bug_description.normalized: OSS-Fuzz issue 39335: uWebSockets TopicTree has a container-overflow read of size 1 in the drainableSubscribers drain path. When the head subscriber of the drainableSubscribers linked list is individually drained via drain(Subscriber *s), the code sets drainableSubscribers to nullptr instead of s->next, orphaning all subsequent subscribers. The orphaned subscribers retain stale messageIndices pointing into the outgoingMessages vector. After a later no-arg drain() clears outgoingMessages, drainImpl accesses the vector at a stale index beyond its current size, causing an ASan container-overflow READ of size 1 when the invalid std::string reference is used.

source.description: The subscriber's message index is materialized from the current outgoingMessages vector size during publish(). This index is valid at creation but becomes a stale out-of-bounds value after the linked-list corruption causes the subscriber to be orphaned and a subsequent drain clears the vector.
source.value_from: The fuzz harness parses PoC bytes into operation chunks and calls topicTree.publish(); inside publish(), the message index is derived from outgoingMessages.size() and stored into the subscriber's messageIndices array.; value `(uint16_t)outgoingMessages.size()`; from `s->messageIndices[s->numMessageIndices++] = (uint16_t)outgoingMessages.size();`

sink.description: drainImpl reads outgoingMessages at the orphaned subscriber's stale message index. The index exceeds the vector's current size (0 after clear) but falls within its allocated capacity. ASan detects the 1-byte read of a std::string in the container-overflow zone when the drain callback calls message.length().

root_cause.description: When the subscriber being individually drained is the head of drainableSubscribers, the code sets drainableSubscribers to nullptr instead of s->next. This orphans all subsequent subscribers in the doubly-linked list: they retain numMessageIndices > 0 and stale messageIndices but are unreachable from the list head. The same bug exists in freeSubscriber at line 233. The patch introduces unlinkDrainableSubscriber() that correctly sets drainableSubscribers to s->next.

tainted_value_origin.description: The message index is recorded from the outgoingMessages vector's current size. It is valid at this point but becomes a stale out-of-bounds index after the vector is cleared while the subscriber is orphaned from the drainableSubscribers list.

coarse_trace.summary: Multiple publishes cause subscribers to accumulate message indices into messageIndices[] and be linked into the drainableSubscribers doubly-linked list.
Single-subscriber drain(s) removes the head subscriber but incorrectly sets drainableSubscribers to nullptr instead of s->next, orphaning all remaining subscribers.
A later no-arg drain() traverses drainableSubscribers (excluding the orphaned subscriber), drains reachable subscribers, and calls outgoingMessages.clear().
Subsequent publishes grow outgoingMessages from zero; the orphaned subscriber accumulates new indices but retains stale indices from before the clear.
When the orphaned subscriber's numMessageIndices reaches 32, publish triggers drain(s) which calls drainImpl, reading outgoingMessages at a stale index beyond the vector's current size.

fine_trace.note: For each subscriber of the published topic, the current outgoingMessages.size() is recorded as a message index. This index is valid now but will become stale if the subscriber is orphaned from drainableSubscribers and outgoingMessages is subsequently cleared.

When a subscriber receives its first message (numMessageIndices transitions to 1), it is inserted at the head of the drainableSubscribers doubly-linked list. Multiple subscribers form a chain: head→A→B→null. The subscriber that will be orphaned (V) is somewhere after the head.

When the head subscriber is individually drained (via publish's numMessageIndices==32 overflow or the fuzzer's drain-one action), this line sets drainableSubscribers to nullptr instead of s->next. All subscribers after the head are orphaned: they retain numMessageIndices > 0 with valid-at-the-time messageIndices but are unreachable from the list head. The patch changes this to drainableSubscribers = s->next.

On subsequent publishes, the orphaned subscriber V receives new message indices (numMessageIndices increments from its orphaned value > 1). Since numMessageIndices != 1, V is not re-inserted into drainableSubscribers and remains orphaned and unreachable for drainage.

A subsequent no-arg drain() is triggered (e.g., by the fuzzer's default action or publish's UINT16_MAX overflow check). It traverses drainableSubscribers, which includes only non-orphaned subscribers (added after the corruption). After draining those, outgoingMessages.clear() resets the vector size to 0 while retaining the allocated capacity. ASan marks the region between size (0) and capacity as container-overflow. The orphaned subscriber V's stale messageIndices now reference positions beyond the vector's valid size.

After accumulating indices across repeated publishes (some stale from before the clear, some newly recorded), V's numMessageIndices reaches 32. publish() calls drain(V) to flush before recording another index. This enters drain(Subscriber *s) which calls drainImpl(V) with V's mixture of stale and valid indices.

drainImpl iterates V's messageIndices. A stale index (recorded before the outgoingMessages.clear() in step 5) references a position beyond the vector's current size but within its allocated capacity. The operator[] returns a reference to a std::string object in ASan's container-overflow zone. The subsequent callback invocation at line 124 passes this reference and calls message.length(), which reads 1 byte from the poisoned region, triggering the ASan container-overflow READ of size 1.

format.name: TopicTree fuzz input (libFuzzer binary blob)
format.contract: Binary blob processed by the makeChunked+makePadded harness into (4-byte subscriber ID, 1-byte action, variable-length topic string) chunks that drive subscribe/publish/drain operations on the TopicTree. The specific byte sequence must produce an interleaving that orphans a subscriber from drainableSubscribers (by draining the list head) and later triggers a drain of the orphaned subscriber after outgoingMessages has been cleared.

parser_admitted.description: The PoC's chunked operations include publish actions with matching topic names, so execution reaches the subscriber iteration loop inside publish() where message indices are recorded and drain is triggered.
